source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Connect BMC Shared port
2. Check BMC netwrok and MAC from Web UI and IPMI OOB "lan print" and check if BMC has only one Bounded LAN chanel
3. Remove BMC Shared port, check BMC network and MAC from Web UI and IPMI OOB command "lan print"
4. Plug BMC Shared port , check BMC network and MAC from Web UI and IPMI OOB command "lan print"
5. To check BMC can display in POST Page.
Optional : 
1. To do WOL in S5, when using sharenic BMC. 

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test
    3. To check BMC IP can display in POST Page
    4. To check WOL successfully and BMC is alive
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. BMC should have same network configuration include IP and MAC in three scenarios
2. BMC network should work in three scenarios
3. DHCP and Static IP should display correctly

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this checks the shared NIC keeps one bound LAN channel across three scenarios (connect, remove, replug) of the BMC shared port. Unplugging/replugging the shared-port cable between scenarios is physical work only a person at the machine can do.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator connects/removes/replugs the BMC shared port and confirms network+MAC stay consistent in each scenario; agent could only read `ipmitool lan print` channel count after the operator switches cabling.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly keeps cable handling manual, but assumes that IP/MAC consistency and network operation are meaningful in all three states without resolving which physical path exists after the shared port is removed. It also omits POST, DHCP-versus-static sequencing and the optional/mandatory WOL conflict.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED correctly identifies the undefined disconnected-state path and separates POST/WOL. Its decision is retained because this is a core topology and acceptance contradiction rather than a missing execution package.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 824/2291 repeats physical-only classification and the source Criteria but does not perform semantic sanity on the impossible or failover-dependent disconnected state.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-988 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently retains its conflict conclusion while expanding the DHCP/static and WOL contradictions and decision ownership.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 prevents missing topology inputs alone from becoming permanent blocks, but ED-36 requires preserving functional coverage. Here the undefined alternate path and contradictory WOL scope change the meaning of success, so an engineer decision is required before execution.

original_test_intent: Validate the BMC shared-NIC binding, channel, MAC/IP configuration and connectivity across connected, physically removed and reconnected shared-port states, also observing POST BMC-IP display and potentially S5 Wake-on-LAN behavior.
original_method: A qualified operator changes the actual shared-port cable state while WebUI and a separately available approved OOB observation path record BMC channel, MAC/IP, DHCP/static display and connectivity; POST and WOL are separate manual/power-state checkpoints. The source does not define the observation/failover path while the shared cable is absent.
manual_activity: Do not execute yet. After the contradictions are resolved, a qualified operator must trace/connect/remove/reconnect the exact shared cable, observe POST, control S5/WOL if selected and restore the approved topology. Automation can then collect per-state channel, identity, reachability and packet evidence.
required_inputs: Authoritative shared-NIC/NC-SI and dedicated-management topology, physical port-to-switch/VLAN map, IPMI channel binding and which path remains available in each state
Explicit connected/removed/reconnected matrix distinguishing configuration persistence, link state and remote reachability, including the observation path during removal
Meaning of `only one Bounded LAN channel`, expected active channel/MAC/IP per state and allowed failover or channel rebinding
Whether DHCP and static are two separate runs or simultaneous display checkpoints, with expected address retention/reacquisition per state

Decision whether POST display is an acceptance checkpoint and whether S5 WOL is optional or mandatory; if WOL is selected, define wake target/source, magic-packet identity, timeout and final power state
Dedicated SUT, maintenance window, alternate/local recovery, protected credentials, cable procedure and evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not remove a management cable until the authoritative topology and recovery path are approved; a hidden dedicated or failover path must not be inferred from an observed response.
Trace the exact chassis shared port, host NIC, switch port, VLAN and MAC before any cable action. Prevent loops, duplicate addresses and accidental removal of the dedicated or production uplink.
Do not treat cached WebUI/IPMI data or retained configuration as live network reachability. Require independent link/path and fresh transaction evidence per state.
Do not use IPMI through the same cable being removed as the only observer. Define a local console, dedicated path or switch-side observer that remains available.
Do not combine DHCP and static results without a defined state transition and restore plan; changing address modes can strand management or produce duplicate IPs.
S5/WOL changes host power state and is not authorized by this static review. No WOL, power transition or automatic retry may occur until separately approved.

Stop on wrong target/path, loop/storm, duplicate address, unexpected channel rebinding, BMC/host loss or unintended wake. Reconnect and secure the cable, restore address/power state and recover locally or through the approved alternate path.
agent_execution_scope: Before an engineer decision, only analyze the topology and acceptance contradictions; do not touch DUT, cable, network or power state.
After approval, collect timestamped per-state link, channel, MAC/IP, lease/static, fresh reachability and service evidence, plus WOL packets/results only if included.
Attribute every response to the exact physical path and distinguish configuration persistence from actual traffic delivery.
Do not recable, observe POST on behalf of the operator, send a magic packet, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Resolve whether removal means physical disconnect with expected loss or failover through a named alternate path, and define the one-bound-channel behavior.
Align the three-state DHCP/static matrix, POST acceptance and optional-versus-mandatory WOL scope without changing the preserved Master source.
Approve and perform the physical/power workflow, restore the platform and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The manual cable boundary is correct, but `lan print` after removing the only shared path is not executable through that same path and cannot resolve the missing topology. No command can repair the semantic contradiction.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No execution command is recommended until engineering defines the removed-state path and scope. Afterwards use vendor-validated channel queries and independent path-bound reachability probes with protected credentials.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Connect/remove/replug, WebUI/IPMI, one bound channel, POST, optional WOL, DHCP/static Criteria and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a state-by-state physical path/channel/IP/MAC/reachability matrix, then run operator-controlled cabling with independent link and fresh-transaction probes; treat POST and WOL as separately selected checkpoints with their own acceptance and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Engineer-approved shared-NIC/NC-SI topology and any named dedicated/failover path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC, NIC/NC-SI, BIOS/POST, switch, DHCP and client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform shared-NIC/NC-SI binding and failover specification, BMC network guide, POST display requirement and Project WOL plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the otherwise undefined disconnected observation path and separate DHCP/static, POST and WOL scopes explicit.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A retained IP/MAC value is not reachability; a dedicated-path response does not prove the unplugged shared path works; WOL cannot be credited when omitted.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer decision on topology, state semantics and optional scope, then execution package.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Choosing an alternate path by inference can make either success or failure support the wrong conclusion and can disrupt the only management route.

project_override_considerations: A Project Override may define an explicit dedicated/failover path or exclude optional WOL, but must record the original three-state/WOL wording, actual topology and method, approval, equivalence and any remaining unverified coverage.
expected_evidence: Engineer-approved shared/dedicated physical and logical topology plus corrected connected/removed/reconnected acceptance matrix
Per-state cable/link/switch/VLAN path evidence and exact BMC/channel/MAC/IP identity
Fresh WebUI/IPMI/network transactions proving configuration persistence versus live reachability, with DHCP and static runs separated as approved
POST BMC-IP display evidence if retained in scope
S5 entry, magic-packet source/target and wake/BMC-alive evidence only if WOL is explicitly selected
Restored cable/address/power state, no loop/duplicate address, retained logs and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure removes the BMC shared port yet immediately asks WebUI/IPMI to check the BMC network, while Criteria require network operation in all three states without defining an alternate path. It also labels WOL optional during the test but requires WOL success after the test, and does not say how DHCP and static both apply.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The removed-state target path and WOL acceptance are core semantics, not merely missing images, tools or expected values. If the shared cable is the only path, reachability should be lost; if another path exists, that path and binding behavior become the function under test. Execution before an engineer decision cannot produce an interpretable verdict.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its physical boundary but rejects its assumption that the three scenarios are already well-defined.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with BLOCKED and strengthens the decision question with one-channel, DHCP/static and WOL scope conflicts.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Adds the missing semantic sanity check and independent observer requirement.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms the conflict and expands its traceable decision and coverage conditions.

review_improvement: Prevents cached configuration or traffic over an unnamed alternate NIC from falsely proving that an unplugged shared link remained functional, and prevents optional WOL from becoming an accidental mandatory power action.
independent_technical_reasoning: A physical link removal changes the only plausible traffic path unless the design provides explicit failover. Therefore the source's success condition is topology-dependent: the same observation can mean correct failover, wrong binding or an impossible expectation. Because the source also contradicts itself on WOL scope, engineering must first define what is actually being accepted.
